extraction.name: COMMONSENSE QA
extraction.description: A challenging new dataset for commonsense question answering containing 12,247 multiple-choice questions that require prior commonsense knowledge, generated from CONCEPTNET.
extraction.creator: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, Jonathan Berant
extraction.publisher: School of Computer Science, Tel-Aviv University; Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Subgraphs are extracted from CONCEPTNET, each with one source concept and three target concepts. Crowd-workers author three questions per subgraph, add two additional distractors per question, and verify question quality. Textual context is added by querying Google search and retrieving web snippets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CONCEPTNET knowledge base and Google search web snippets.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Triplets from CONCEPTNET were filtered to remove general relations, relations already well-explored in NLP, concepts with more than four words, non-English concepts, and triplets where the edit distance between the question concept and answer concept is too low.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A web query was issued to Google search for every question and candidate answer, concatenating the answer to the question. The first 100 result snippets for each of the five answer candidates were taken, yielding a context of 500 snippets per question.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: AMT workers were shown a question concept and three answer concepts. They formulated three questions containing the question concept, each having one of the answer concepts as the correct answer. Workers were instructed to avoid using words with a strong relation to the answer concept. Workers also added two distractors per question: one selected from CONCEPTNET and one formulated manually.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A disjoint group of workers verified the generated questions by annotating them as unanswerable or choosing the right answer. Only questions verified by at least one worker that answered correctly were used, filtering out 15% of the questions.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each question is verified by 2 workers.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Networks that memorize might fail on the random split because the same question concept appears in the training set and development/test set with different answer concepts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation (Data is split into a training/development/test set with an 80/10/10 split).
